_comment: Curated demo board for the documentation screenshots (scripts/docs-shots.sh). Fictional repos/branches only — never the user's real work. Each entry is spawned through the ISOLATED daemon's `orchestra` CLI, so every card is a genuine worktree running a genuine agent; nothing here is faked telemetry. Keep the prompts small and bounded: they run for real and they bill.
_notes: `col` is the card's FINAL column. `spawn --col` is start-only (plan|impl by design), so a `review` card is spawned into impl and then moved with `orchestra move` — the same two steps a human would take. The codex card picks its backend via `model` (the agent is inferred from the model id). Cards are told not to move themselves: the SessionStart orientation nudges an agent to move its own card as work changes phase, which is right in real use but empties the Review column mid-screenshot. Columns are RE-APPLIED right before the stills: agents move their own cards (the SessionStart orientation tells them to), so the board drifts from the fixture during the work window. Implementation is left holding only the pagination card so `g i` selects it deterministically for the inspector/diff shots. The reviewer card sets `attachBranch` instead of its own `branch` — the drive script spawns it `--cwd <the pagination card's worktree> --read-only` (a branchless, borrowed reviewer; `orchestra spawn` only threads `--read-only` through the `--cwd` path today, not `--repo`/`--branch`, so this is the CLI-supported way to attach one) so it hangs off the pagination card by directory match. That makes the pagination card a hierarchy root with a live attached-agents eye — without it none of the board-hierarchy/attachment UI has anything to render. Its `col` is `impl` (matching its spawn start), never `review`: a read-only reviewer always embeds behind its target and never becomes its own column card, so unlike the worktree cards above it must NOT be `move`d after spawn — the daemon rejects a column move on a freeform-origin card outright.

api.desc: a small HTTP service — the repo most demo cards work in

# infra

Terraform and CI for the api/web services.
files.ci/pipeline.yml:
steps:
  - name: test
    run: npm test
  - name: build
    run: npm run build

cards.prompt: In src/theme.css, add a dark colour scheme behind a prefers-color-scheme media query, reusing the existing custom properties. Keep it to that one file. Do not run any orchestra CLI commands, and do not move this card between columns.

Add a small cursor-based pagination helper to src/ (a new file plus a couple of routes wired into src/server.js). Keep it under ~60 lines total. Also write a short notes/pagination.md (under 15 lines) explaining the cursor format for a reviewer. Write the code and doc only — do not start the server, curl it, or run any other shell commands to test it.
Read the pagination helper and notes/pagination.md, then report anything you'd want changed before merge. Do not edit any files, and do not move this card.
Add a dependency-cache step to ci/pipeline.yml, keyed on the lockfile. One file, a few lines. Leave this card in the Review column — do not move it.
Read src/store.js and write a short plan (notes/plan.md) for moving it behind a redis-backed interface. Plan only — do not change any source.

orchestrator.prompt: You are orchestrating the rate-limiting work for this repo from an Orchestra board. You can drive the board either with the `orchestra` MCP tools or with the `orchestra` CLI (it is on your PATH and already points at this board) — they are the same commands. Read src/server.js and src/store.js so you know the codebase, then STOP and wait for instructions — do not change any code yourself.
orchestrator.nudge: Split the rate-limiting work into three PRs and fan them out — one card each for the core token-bucket limiter, the redis-backed store, and the tests. Spawn them with your orchestra MCP tools (same repo, a branch each). If the MCP tools are unavailable, use the CLI instead — it is equivalent: orchestra spawn --prompt "..." --repo /private/tmp/orch-docs/api --branch feat/<name> --col impl. Then wait on them.
